chapter: Dave and Iola: faith and values
title: How Dave came to Catholicism and writing the Mass 'To Hope'
summary: Chris tells of Dave's interest in religious teachers and a dream that completed his Mass; Monk adds the story of 'God's Love Made Visible'.

story.theme_name: Church, faith and religion in a musician's life
story.community_name: Church, faith and jazz: the sacred and the secular

blocks.x: Oh you know what? And I never quite — you brought up the question of how did Dave become a Catholic. And it’s a very interesting story. So he’s always been interested in Jesus and all these different religions. There’s times in our lives where Dan, mainly, he was the prime mover like the couple of times we took Dave to meet, you know like an Eastern religious leader like a Baba Muktananda or Baba Hari Dass, or these different people. So yeah, he had an open mind. And you know one of the things I think it was Hari Dass said, and you can correct me, Dan, if I’m wrong. But you know there’s many paths to seek enlightenment but his analogy which always made a hell of a lot of sense to me is you can keep exploring this and exploring that and exploring this. But if you ever want to get up to the mountaintop of whatever path you choose religiously you’ve got to stick with one or you’ll just keep jumping and jumping and never get anywhere. So when Dave wrote his beautiful mass called “To Hope” he left out — for some weird reason because it’s a very structured thing what goes into a concert mass, from hundreds of years of tradition in Catholic church music — he left out the “Our Father.” And one morning he — it’s a beautiful, beautiful — if you hear it, it’s gorgeous and it just sounds like it couldn’t be written any other way, like each note deserves to follow the next. You know it’s just one of those that fell out of the sky perfect. And he dreamed that. And it was one of those dreams where he went, “Oh I’m dreaming. I want to write that down before I forget.” So he wrote it down. And it’s beautiful, it went to the mass. And for Dave the final straw for making him commit to one religion to get to enlightenment was he thought well God showed me and gave me that piece. And that was it.

Wow. That reminds me of a story both Dave and Iola told me about being in a van like a VW type van driving up to summer camp in Vermont, music camp. And that’s when “God’s Love Made Visible” was written.
Oh yeah. Probably driving Matthew to Kinhaven.

I think you’re right. That’s what he said. And Dave said, “I’m done with this” and she said, “No you’re not.” And I’ll have to show you, like I’m telling you a story about your father that you don’t know I guess. And then he went up and got up there and they were put up in an A frame and up in the top attic were all the Christmas decorations so he went up there and finished it. It’s just very touching.
